item.title: How to Monitor Your Crystal/Lucky Framework Application with Vigilmon
item.author: Vigilmon
item.content:encoded:
Crystal and the Lucky web framework give you Ruby-like syntax with C-level performance. But fast code still needs uptime monitoring. This guide shows you how to set up production monitoring for your Crystal/Lucky app with Vigilmon.
Why Monitor a Crystal App Externally? Crystal compiles to native binaries with no runtime overhead. But your app can still go down:Segfault or unhandled exception crashes the processDatabase connection pool exhaustionMemory leak in a C extensionReverse proxy (nginx/Caddy) misconfiguration after a deployExternal monitoring catches all of these — Vigilmon checks your actual HTTP endpoint from outside, exactly as users do. — checks your Lucky app's public URL every minute — tracks how fast pages load across multiple regions — alerts 30 days before your certificate expires — detects 500 errors, redirect loops, or unexpected responses — for Lucky background jobs (e.g., periodic tasks)
Step 1: Add a Health Check Endpoint First, add a lightweight health route to your Lucky app:This route bypasses your app's auth pipeline and returns a simple 200 response.curl http://localhost:5000/health
Step 2: Add Vigilmon Monitor Enter your Lucky app's health URL: https://yourapp.com/healthSet check interval: Add alert contacts (email, Slack, PagerDuty)Vigilmon immediately starts checking from multiple geographic regions.
Step 3: SSL Certificate Monitoring Add a second monitor for SSL:Click → select Enter your domain: Set expiry threshold: You'll get an alert with enough time to renew before expiry causes downtime.
Step 4: Monitor Background Jobs (Heartbeat) If your Lucky app runs periodic tasks — cron-style jobs using or an external scheduler — add a heartbeat monitor:In Vigilmon, create a Copy the unique ping URL (e.g., https://vigilmon.online/ping/abc123)In your scheduled task, ping that URL each time it runs: If your job fails or stops running, Vigilmon detects the missed heartbeat and alerts you.Vigilmon supports multiple alert channels: — instant notification to your team — posts to your ops channel — for on-call rotation — any custom endpointFor Lucky apps in production, set up Slack + email at minimum.
Checking Your Monitor Dashboard After setup, your Vigilmon dashboard shows: over 24h / 7d / 30d with regional breakdown — every outage logged with start/end time
Why Crystal/Lucky Apps Need External Monitoring Lucky's type-safe approach catches many bugs at compile time, but production failures still happen. Common Crystal production issues:Yes — response time spike + timeoutDatabase connection errorYes — certificate monitorYes — immediate HTTP check failureSetting up Vigilmon for your Crystal/Lucky app takes under 5 minutes:Add endpoint to your Lucky appAdd HTTP uptime monitor in VigilmonAdd SSL certificate monitorAdd heartbeat monitors for background jobsConfigure Slack/email alertsVigilmon handles external monitoring so you know immediately when something breaks — whether it's a deploy gone wrong, a process crash, or a cert about to expire.Monitor your Crystal/Lucky app in production with Vigilmon — free to start.

item.title: Building a real-time Crystal app with Kemal — where privacy is a server invariant
item.author: David YOTEAU
item.content:encoded:
I'm building , a suite of small self-hosted team-ritual tools. There's a twist: each app deliberately uses a framework, to make one point over and over — framework choice should match problem size, not habit.The first one to ship is : a facilitator opens a session, participants join with a short code and privately rank ten motivation cards, and when everyone's ready the facilitator triggers a so all rankings appear side by side for discussion.Two properties make it interesting: State lives in memory and nowhere else. Sessions expire after a few hours and get swept. No database, no ORM, no migrations. A participant's ranking must stay hidden from the others until the reveal. Not "the UI hides it" — the server must never put another participant's ranking in a payload before that moment.That second property is the one that shaped the whole design. Let's build it.Kemal is a Sinatra-style micro-framework: routes, a request/response cycle, WebSockets, static files. That's the entire feature list — and it's exactly the feature list this app needs.There's no database, so an ORM would be dead weight. There's no asset build, so a pipeline would be ceremony. The rule I hold throughout: the framework is an adapter. All the actual rules of the game live in plain Crystal objects that never import Kemal. That's what lets me test the whole domain without booting a
1. The domain, framework-free Start with the smallest certain thing and build up. A isn't "a list of cards" — it's a complete ordering of all ten, no duplicates, no gaps. Make that a value object that enforces its own invariants at construction, so an invalid ranking simply can't exist:Because construction validates, every other method can trust the invariant — uses (the raising variant) with no nil check, and that's safe.The owns a two-phase state machine — → — and it's terminal: you don't un-reveal a group discussion. It guards every mutation, so noThe session never calls the clock itself — the caller passes the current time in, which keeps expiry logic deterministic and trivial to test.
2. Confidentiality as a server invariant Here's the chapter that justifies the architecture.The requirement isn't "hide other rankings in the UI." It's "the server must never another participant's ranking before reveal." So I build the exact view a given participant is allowed to see, and I build it — the one place a forgetful route handler can't bypass:A ranking makes it into the view only when the session is revealed it's the viewer's own. Everyone else's is . Because confidentiality is decided , no downstream layer has to remember to enforce it — the serializer and the WebSocket hub just faithfully transmit whatever the view contains. Note what the view : the participant's is their secret WebSocket token, so it marks the viewer with a plain flag rather than handing every client everyone else's credentials.And I test the wire directly, with belt and suspenders — not only should a hidden ranking be , no card name from it may appear anywhere in the bytes:
3. Real time with a WebSocket hub After joining, every state change travels over a WebSocket. The subtle part is the push: a single broadcast must produce a payload per viewer, because each viewer may see different things. So the hub sends every socket its:Two robustness details earn their place: the lock is held only long enough to copy the connection list — never across a blocking , or one slow client would stall every session on the server — and a broken socket raises , caught per connection so one dropped client can't cut off the rest of the room.Confidentiality is not re-implemented here. The hub trusts the view; the view already withheld what must stay secret. That's the payoff of step 2.The highest-value test in the suite boots a server and drives two live sockets end to end, proving confidentiality on the actual wire:
4. A hardened 14 MB image, Crystal compiles to a single native binary, so the container can be tiny. I borrow the approach fromspider-gazelle's Dockerfile: build a linked binary, then ship exactly the shared libraries says it needs — so each library is patchable independently, and a scanner sees real package versions instead of one opaque static blob.The trick is one that walks the binary's dependencies and copies each into a tree mirroring its absolute path:binary /app/bin/ ldd | | | xargs % sh For this app that's seven libraries — the musl loader, OpenSSL, the GC,, PCRE2 and zlib. The final stage is with just the identity files, those libraries, the binary and the assets — and it runs as an:Port 3000 is above 1024, so the non-root user binds it with no extra capability. The result is ~14 MB — a few MB more than a fully static build, traded for a non-root, patchable-libs posture.docker run 3000:3000 ghcr.io/jadekharats/motivators:latest
How good are the tests, really? Line coverage tells you which lines ran. It doesn't tell you whether your assertions would catch a bug. So I ran crytic mutation testing on the domain — and even with a green suite, it surfaced three real assertion gaps. My favourite: mutating to produced an , meaning would authorise. No spec caught it. A genuine security hole that coverage was blind to.After closing the gaps, the domain sits at , and CI runs an incremental mutation gate on every pull request.The finished app is ~290 lines of Crystal plus a single-file, no-build frontend. No database, no ORM, no pipeline. It does exactly what a half-hour team ritual needs and not one thing more — and keeping it that small is the feature.It has one honest limit: state lives in a single process, so it runs as . For this problem, that's the right trade; scaling out behind a shared pub/sub is a possible extension, not the default. Reaching for it before you need it would be exactly the over-engineering the whole Happy suite argues against.Next in the series: , where the problem call for a bigger tool — auth, uploads, history — and so it's built on Lucky. Same lesson, opposite conclusion. That's the point.If you'd right-size differently, I'd genuinely like to hear it — tell me in the comments.Thanks to @renich for spotting that the participant id — which doubles as the secret WebSocket token — was being broadcast in the session view, and for the first fix. The -flag approach in the confidentiality section is what closed it.

item.title: Stop Coding PDF Layouts: How to Build Clean Templates Visually
item.author: TommyDev
item.content:encoded:
If you've ever had to build dynamic PDF documents—invoices, shipping labels, compliance reports, or receipts—you know the pain. Usually, developers end up down one of two painful paths: Using low-level PDF libraries (like PDFKit, FPDF, or TCPDF) where adding a simple border or moving an image 10px down means tweaking coordinate arrays and re-running backend code 50 times. Using headless browsers (Puppeteer, WKHTMLTOPDF) that consume gigabytes of RAM on your server and break pagination the moment a table spans across two pages.There is a much cleaner architectural approach: separating the document design from your application logic.
The Core Concept: Visual Design + JSON Payload When building web applications, you wouldn't mix your CSS directly into your database queries. So why mix PDF visual design into your backend controllers?By decoupling the template design from the rendering execution, your workflow transforms into two simple steps: Create and tweak headers, dynamic tables, page numbers, logos, and conditional visibility in a visual drag-and-drop editor. Send a clean JSON payload with your dynamic data to an API endpoint that handles the heavy rendering lifting.
How the QuartzAPI Visual Builder Solves This This design-first methodology is the core engine behind QuartzAPI. Instead of writing lines of boilerplate code to handle page breaks, repeating table headers, or dynamic text wrapping, the lets you construct document templates visually directly in the browser:Drag-and-Drop Components: Place text boxes, images, dynamic data fields, and barcodes exactly where you need them. Define repeating rows for line items that automatically handle multi-page overflow and header repetition cleanly. Bind visual fields directly to your JSON schema variables using simple syntax. Test how your template renders with real sample JSON payloads before sending a single HTTP request from your app.
What the Code Actually Looks Like Once your template is saved in the builder, generating a complex, multi-page PDF from your backend (Node.js, PHP, Python, C#, etc.) becomes as simple as sending a standard POST request.Here is an example payload:{ "template_id": "tpl_invoice_v2", "invoice_number": "INV-2026-089", "name": "Acme Corp", }, { "description": "Cloud API Subscription", "qty": 1, "price": 49.00 }, { "description": "Custom Integration Support", "qty": 2, "price": 150.00 } ], }Your backend application doesn't care about page dimensions, fonts, or margin calculations. It just supplies the raw data—QuartzAPI handles the rest and returns the generated PDF.
Why Decoupling Matters for Teams Shifting PDF generation to a visual builder + REST API architecture brings massive benefits: Your application server doesn't freeze or run out of memory spawning headless browser processes.Faster Design Iterations: Need to update the company logo, change a color scheme, or adjust footer legal text? Update the template in the visual builder without redeploying your backend code. Keep your backend clean, focused purely on business logic and data retrieval.If your team is still spending expensive engineering hours wrestling with PDF layouts or maintaining bloated legacy reporting servers, it’s time to modernize the stack.Check out QuartzAPI to try out the visual builder and see how effortless document generation can be.What tools are you currently using for PDF generation in production? Let's discuss in the comments below!

item.title: Best Free Image Converter Online
item.author: Mirza Salman
item.content:encoded:
You've probably run into this before: a website only accepts WebP, your design tool exports PNG, and the form you're filling out insists on JPG. Every format has its own use case, but that also means you end up needing to convert between them more often than you'd expect - and most operating systems don't make that a one-click task without opening some kind of editor first. A simple online image converter solves this without any of the overhead. Upload the file you have, pick the format you need, and download the result.The Image Converter is a free browser-based tool that converts images between PNG, JPG, and WebP formats. You upload your file, choose the target format, and the tool converts it and shows you the resulting file size - all without leaving the page or creating an account.It's a focused tool: it doesn't try to also resize, crop, or filter your image. It just handles the format conversion cleanly, which is often exactly the single step you need in the middle of a larger workflow.Format conversion sounds minor until you're the one stuck without the right tool:Supports the three formats that matter most. PNG, JPG, and WebP cover the vast majority of everyday image needs - from transparency-friendly graphics to universally compatible photos to modern, web-optimized files.Shows the new file size immediately. You're not left guessing whether converting to a different format helped or hurt your file size - the tool tells you right after conversion.Runs privately in your browser. The conversion happens on your device, so you're not sending images to an unknown server just to change their format. Upload, convert, download - there's no account wall in between. There's no cap on how many images you can convert or a paywall hiding the download button.If you just need a file in a different format for the next five minutes, this is a much faster path than opening a full editor.Converting an image takes just a few steps: The tool accepts PNG, JPG, and WebP files.Choose your target format. Pick whichever of the three formats you need the output to be. The conversion happens locally, and you'll see the resulting file size once it's done.Download the converted file. Grab your new file in the format you selected.There's one detail worth understanding before you convert: JPG has no support for transparency. If you convert a transparent PNG to JPG, any transparent areas in the original image will be filled with white in the output, since JPG simply doesn't have a way to represent "no color here." This is standard behavior for any PNG-to-JPG conversion, not a quirk of this specific tool - it's just how the JPG format works. If you need to keep transparency, PNG or WebP are the formats to stick with.Format conversion comes up in more situations than you'd think:Meeting a platform's format requirement. Some upload forms, CMS platforms, or ad networks only accept specific formats, and converting your existing file is faster than re-exporting from the original source.Shrinking web page weight with WebP. WebP files are often meaningfully smaller than equivalent PNGs or JPGs at similar visual quality, which makes converting existing image assets to WebP a quick way to trim a website's load time.Preparing images for older or stricter systems. Some tools, print services, or legacy systems only work reliably with JPG or PNG, and won't accept newer formats like WebP.Converting screenshots or graphics for documents. Screenshots are often saved as PNG by default, and converting to JPG can be useful when you need a smaller file for something like a report or presentation where transparency doesn't matter.Standardizing a mixed batch of assets. If you've collected images from different sources in different formats, converting them all to one consistent format makes them easier to manage and use together.Testing how an image looks or performs in a different format. Sometimes you just want to compare file size or quality between PNG, JPG, and WebP versions of the same image before deciding which to actually use.Keep these points in mind to avoid surprises:Convert PNG to JPG only when transparency doesn't matter. Remember that any transparent pixels will be filled with white, so this works well for photos but poorly for logos or graphics that rely on a transparent background.Use WebP when your priority is web performance. If the target is a website and the platform supports WebP, it's often the smallest of the three formats for a given level of visual quality.Use PNG when you need transparency or crisp edges. Logos, icons, and graphics with sharp lines or transparent backgrounds are usually best kept as PNG.Use JPG for maximum compatibility. If you're not sure what a destination supports, JPG is the safest, most universally recognized format for photographic content.Check the resulting file size before assuming you've made things smaller. Converting formats doesn't automatically guarantee a smaller file - check the size the tool shows you after conversion to confirm it actually helped. If you convert a PNG with transparency to JPG and later realize you needed the transparency back, you'll want the original PNG on hand rather than trying to recreate it from the JPG.
Frequently Asked Questions
Which formats can I convert between? You can convert between PNG, JPG, and WebP in any direction - upload one of these formats and choose any of the other two (or the same one) as your target.
What happens to transparency when I convert a PNG to JPG? Since JPG doesn't support transparency, any transparent areas in your original PNG will be filled with white in the converted JPG.
Does converting to WebP always make the file smaller? Not always, but WebP is generally efficient and often produces smaller files than PNG or JPG at similar quality. The tool shows you the resulting file size after conversion so you can confirm.
Is my image uploaded to a server for conversion? No, the conversion runs in your browser, so your image doesn't need to leave your device.
Do I need an account to use the converter? No, there's no signup required - you can upload, convert, and download right away.
Can I convert a JPG to PNG to add transparency back? Converting a JPG to PNG changes the file format, but it can't recreate transparency that was already lost - if the JPG has a solid white (or other) background where transparency used to be, that background stays as-is after conversion.
Which format should I use for a logo? PNG is usually the best choice for logos, especially if you need a transparent background or crisp, sharp edges.Whenever you need a file in a different format, skip the design software and use the Image Converter. Upload your image, pick PNG, JPG, or WebP, and download the converted file in seconds.

item.title: Funeral Home in Denver: A Complete Guide for Families
item.author: Subyarth Craft Pvt Ltd
item.content:encoded: Losing someone you love is one of life's hardest moments. During this time, finding a trusted Funeral Home in Denver can help make the process easier. A caring funeral home guides families through every step, from planning the service to handling important arrangements. Whether you choose a traditional funeral, cremation, or a simple memorial service, the right team provides support with kindness and respect.Denver has many funeral homes that serve families from different backgrounds, cultures, and faiths. Many also offer personalized services that help celebrate the life of your loved one in a meaningful way.Why Choosing the Right Funeral Home MattersA funeral home does much more than arrange a ceremony. It helps families make important decisions during an emotional time. Experienced funeral directors explain your options clearly, handle paperwork, and make sure every detail is taken care of.When looking for a funeral home, choose one that offers:Compassionate and experienced staff Clear pricing with no hidden costs Burial and cremation services Memorial planning Support before and after the serviceTaking time to compare funeral homes can help you find one that matches your family's needs and budget.What Services Do Funeral Homes in Denver Offer?Most funeral homes in Denver provide a wide range of services to help families honor their loved ones.Traditional Funeral ServicesTraditional funerals usually include a visitation, funeral ceremony, transportation, and burial. Families can choose religious or non-religious services based on their wishes.Many families today choose cremation because it offers flexibility and can be more affordable than a traditional burial. Funeral homes often provide direct cremation, memorial ceremonies, and assistance with selecting a beautiful urn for ashes to preserve your loved one's memory.Memorial and Celebration of Life ServicesA celebration of life focuses on remembering happy moments and honoring a person's unique journey. Families often include photos, favorite music, videos, and personal stories to create a meaningful tribute.How to Choose the Best Funeral Home in DenverChoosing the right funeral home becomes easier when you know what to look for.Check Reviews and ReputationRead online reviews and ask friends or family for recommendations. Positive feedback often shows that a funeral home provides caring service and professional support.Compare Prices and ServicesFuneral costs can vary. Request a price list and compare service packages before making a decision. A good funeral home explains every cost clearly.Look for Personalized OptionsEvery family is different. Many funeral homes offer custom memorial services, engraved keepsakes, memory tables, video tributes, and personalized urns for ashes to honor your loved one in a special way.Understanding Cremation and Memorial OptionsCremation has become a popular choice because it gives families more flexibility when planning a memorial.Choosing the Right Urn for AshesSelecting the right urn for ashes helps keep your loved one's memory close. Urns come in different materials, colors, and designs. Many families choose personalized urns with names, dates, or meaningful messages engraved on them.A quality urn provides a lasting tribute while becoming a beautiful part of a home memorial.Dog Urn and Cat Urn for Beloved PetsPets are family too. Losing a loyal dog or a loving cat can be just as heartbreaking. Many families choose a Dog Urn or Cat Urn to remember the happy moments they shared with their beloved companion.Personalized pet urns allow you to add your pet's name, dates, or a special message. They offer a comforting way to keep your pet's memory close for years to come.Planning ahead can reduce stress and give your family peace of mind.Pre-planning allows you to make important decisions before they are needed. You can choose your preferred funeral service, cremation option, memorial style, and budget. This also helps your family avoid making difficult decisions during an emotional time.Grief affects everyone differently. Spend time together, share memories, and don't hesitate to seek support from grief counselors or local support groups. Many funeral homes in Denver also provide grief resources to help families through the healing process.Finding the right Funeral Home in Denver is an important step in honoring the life of someone you love. A trusted funeral home provides guidance, compassion, and professional care while helping families create meaningful memories. Whether you choose burial, cremation, or a celebration of life, thoughtful planning brings comfort during a difficult time.If you are considering cremation, choosing a beautiful urn for ashes can create a lasting tribute. Families who have lost a beloved pet can also honor their faithful companions with a personalized Dog Urn or Cat Urn, keeping treasured memories close every day.How do I choose the best funeral home in Denver?Look for experienced staff, transparent pricing, positive customer reviews, and services that match your family's needs.What services do funeral homes in Denver provide?They offer traditional funerals, cremation services, memorial ceremonies, pre-planning, transportation, and grief support.Can I personalize an urn for ashes?Yes. Many urns can be engraved with names, dates, quotes, or special messages.Are Dog Urns and Cat Urns available in personalized designs?Yes. Many pet urns can be customized with your pet's name, photo, paw print, or a heartfelt message.Is cremation more affordable than burial?In many cases, cremation costs less than a traditional burial, but the final price depends on the services and memorial options you choose.

item.title: I Spent 6 Months Working With Chakra Stones — Here's What Actually Happened
item.author: Kui Luo
item.content:encoded:
About seven months ago, I was sleeping maybe four hours a night. Not because of insomnia exactly — more like my brain just refused to shut down. I'd tried melatonin, magnesium supplements, cutting screen time after 9pm. Nothing stuck. A friend who runs a wellness studio in Austin suggested I look into chakra stones. I was skeptical. I'm a data analyst by training — I don't believe in things I can't measure.But I was desperate enough to try anything.So I bought a set of seven crystals aligned with the seven chakras and committed to actually using them daily for six months. No skipping days. I kept a sleep journal, tracked my energy levels on a 1-10 scale every morning, and noted any changes in mood or focus. Here's what I found.
Month 1: Starting With the Root I started with root chakra stones — specifically black tourmaline and red jasper. The idea is that your root chakra governs your sense of safety and groundedness. Without it being balanced, everything above it is supposedly unstable too.The first two weeks, nothing happened. I put the stones under my pillow at night and carried black tourmaline in my pocket during the day. I felt like I was performing a ritual for no reason. My sleep score averaged 4.2/10 for the first 14 days, tracked via my Oura ring.Around day 18, something shifted. I noticed I was falling asleep about 20 minutes faster than before. Not earth-shattering, but consistent. By the end of month one, my average sleep score had crept up to 5.6/10.Was it the stones or just placebo? Honestly, I still don't know. But I kept going.
Months 2-3: The Sacral and Solar Plexus Experiment Here's the thing nobody tells you about crystal work: the routine itself becomes a form of mindfulness. Ten minutes in the morning holding a warm carnelian stone, focusing on my breathing, became a ritual I actually looked forward to. I wasn't just "playing with rocks" — I was meditating. The stone was just an anchor.During these two months, my energy levels (self-reported, 1-10 scale) averaged 6.8, up from 5.1 in the first month. I also noticed I was less reactive to stressful situations at work. Whether that's the crystals, the meditation, or just me getting better at handling stress, the outcome was real.
Month 4: The Heart Chakra Shift I've always had a hard time with vulnerability. Green aventurine and rose quartz were the recommended heart chakra crystals. I placed rose quartz on my chest during my evening meditation for the entire month.This one surprised me. By week three, I had a conversation with my partner about something I'd been avoiding for literally two years. I can't attribute that entirely to a pink stone, but the consistent practice of sitting with my chest, breathing, and focusing on openness seemed to create space for honesty I hadn't accessed before.
Months 5-6: Third Eye and Crown I added amethyst and clear quartz for the third eye chakra. This was the most subtle phase. I didn't notice dramatic shifts, but I did start having more vivid dreams and felt generally more intuitive about small decisions — like knowing which project to prioritize at work.My final averages for month 6:Sleep score: 7.3/10 (up from 4.2)Energy level: 7.6/10 (up from 5.1)Self-reported stress: 3.2/10 (down from 7.8)Look, I can't tell you crystals have magical properties. What I can tell you is this: the practice of working with them created a daily meditation habit that measurably improved my sleep, energy, and stress levels. The stones themselves may be incidental. Or they may not be. I'm not qualified to say.What I am qualified to say is that I spent about $85 total on my crystal set, and the return on that investment — six months of better sleep, lower stress, and a consistent mindfulness practice — is hard to argue with.If you're curious but skeptical like I was, the best beginner resource I found was this guide. It breaks down each chakra, which stones correspond to it, and how to actually start using them without falling into the "buy everything at once" trap.One piece of advice I wish someone had given me: start with just one stone for one chakra. Don't buy a whole set. Pick the area of your life that needs the most attention — sleep, confidence, emotional balance — and work with that single stone for at least a month before adding more.I started with black tourmaline for my root chakra. It was the right call. Six months later, I still sleep with it under my pillow most nights.
